On the 21st, Hong Kong’s South China Morning Post (SCMP), citing data from Thailand’s Board of Investment, reported that the Thai government approved 321 investment projects involving mainland Chinese capital in the first half of this year.
This accounts for a quarter of all investment projects. The 321 projects were valued at 9.7 billion yuan (about 1.9 trillion won).
From 2021 to 2025, cumulative mainland Chinese investment in Thailand totaled 132.5 billion yuan (about 26.3 trillion won), with an average annual growth rate of 56%.
The trend is also borne out by Chinese data. According to China’s Ministry of Commerce, Chinese investment secured by Thailand last year totaled $5.33 billion (about 7.06 trillion won), far exceeding Vietnam’s $2.46 billion.
This is seen as indicating that Chinese companies are adopting a “China Plus One” strategy, shifting investment from their home market to neighboring countries, and favoring Thailand over Vietnam.
Donald Low, a professor in the Department of Public Policy at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, told SCMP, “Infrastructure bottlenecks and rising labor costs are making Vietnam less attractive as a destination for manufacturing investment.” He added, “By contrast, Thailand has a mature and sophisticated manufacturing base.”
Many Chinese companies now operate in Thailand, including automakers such as BYD, Changan Automobile and Chery, home appliance makers such as Haier and Midea, and solar companies such as Trina Solar.
